angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 244,191 km at 127.23 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.8599 +/- 0.0461 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 127.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.351 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Kanodia et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7149 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..203K/abstract): 244,191 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.344 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Kanodia et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7149 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..203K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3363 +/- 59 K from Kanodia et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7149 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..203K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kanodia et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7149 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..203K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7149.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.884, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
